To reduce the risk of SEVERE INJURY OR DEATH FROM COLLISIONS:
SCAN CONSTANTLY for people, objects, and other watercraft. Be alert for conditions that limit your visibility or block your vision of others.
OPERATE DEFENSIVELY at safe speeds and keep a safe distance from people, objects, and other watercraft.
- Do not follow directly behind other watercraft.
- Do not go near others to spray or splash them with water.
- Avoid sharp turns or other maneuvers that make it hard for others to avoid you or understand where you are going.
- Avoid areas with submerged objects or shallow water.
TAKE EARLY ACTION to avoid collisions. Remember, boats do not have brakes.
DO NOT PULL THROTTLE LEVERS BACK TO IDLE WHEN TRYING TO STEER away from objects - you need throttle to steer. Always check throttle, shift, and steering controls for proper operation before starting boat.
Follow navigation rules and state and local laws that apply to your boat.
See Owner's Manual for more information.

YAMAHA
FOR-U416C-21 WARNING

Do not use reverse function to slow down or stop boat above trolling speed as it could cause you to lose control, be ejected, or impact boat surfaces.

Reverse is for low speed maneuvering only.
Shift only while engine is idling or off.

YAMAHA
F2G-U415D-00 WARNING

Carbon monoxide (CO) can cause brain damage or death.
Engine exhaust contains odorless and colorless carbon monoxide gas.
Signs of carbon monoxide poisoning include nausea, headache, dizziness, drowsiness, and lack of consciousness.
Get fresh air if anyone shows signs of carbon monoxide poisoning.
See Owner's Manual for information regarding carbon monoxide poisoning.

YAMAHA
F3A-U415P-00 WARNING

To reduce the risk of SEVERE INJURY OR DEATH:

WEAR A COAST GUARD-APPROVED PERSONAL FLOTATION DEVICE (PFD).

KNOW BOATING LAWS. Yamaha recommends a minimum operation age of 16 years old. Know the operator age and training requirements for your state. A boating safety course is recommended and may be required in your state.

ATTACH ENGINE SHUT-OFF CORD (LANYARD) to your PFD and keep it free of controls so the engines stop if the operator leaves the helm. Failure to attach engine shut-off cord could result in a runaway boat if operator is ejected. After operation, remove engine shut-off cord and keys from boat to avoid unauthorized use by children or others.

BE SURE SHIFT CONTROL IS IN NEUTRAL before starting engines.

OPERATE WITHIN YOUR LIMITS AND AVOID AGGRESSIVE MANEUVERS to reduce the risk of loss of control, ejection, and collision. This is a high-performance boat - not a toy. Sharp turns or jumping wakes or waves can increase the risk of back/spinal injury (paralysis), facial injuries, and broken legs, ankles, and other bones. Do not jump wakes or waves.

DO NOT APPLY THROTTLE WHEN ANYONE IS AT REAR OF BOAT - turn engines off while boarding from the rear, using the swim platform, or when swimming behind the boat. Water and/or debris exiting the jet thrust nozzles can cause severe injury including severe internal injuries if water is forced into body cavities (rectum and vagina).

KEEP AWAY FROM INTAKE GRATES while engines are on. Items such as long hair, loose clothing, or PFD straps can become entangled in moving parts resulting in severe injury or drowning.

NEVER RIDE AFTER CONSUMING DRUGS OR ALCOHOL.

READ AND FOLLOW OWNER'S MANUAL.

YAMAHA
F1C-U416C-10 NOTICE

TO AVOID LOSS OF PERFORMANCE OR BOAT DAMAGE CAUSED BY LOST ACCESS PORT CAP:

Access Port Cap Removal
- Be sure retaining cord is securely attached to cap and strap eye.
- While holding handle and pushing down, turn cap counterclockwise until "SET" mark is aligned with slot (A).
- Lift cap by handle.

Do not lift or pull cap with cord.

Access Port Cap Installation
- Before reinstalling cap in access port, clean off any sand or other foreign matter on cap or port surfaces.
- Insert cap so that "SET" mark is aligned with slot (A).
- Turn cap clockwise until "SET" mark is aligned with arrow (B).
- Check cap - if handle is not perpendicular to centerline of boat or a strong pull will move cap, it is not locked securely and could be forced out by water pressure.

Diagram labels: B, A, Perpendicular to centerline, SET

WARNING

SEVERE INJURY OR DEATH MAY RESULT IF YOU IGNORE ANY OF THE FOLLOWING.
- Turn off and remove both ignition keys, remove lanyard, and wait for all movement to stop before removing access port caps.
- Never override interlocks to run engines with hatch open.

Label code: F3F-U411D-00 WARNING

Falling Hazard.

Falling on the deck or overboard may cause injury or death.

Do not sit here when the boat is moving.

YAMAHA

F1C-U418C-00 WARNING

Severe internal injuries can occur if water is forced into body cavities (rectum and vagina) as a result of being near jet thrust nozzles.

- Do not board from rear, use swim platform, or swim behind boat if engine(s) is running.
- When water-skiing, wear a wet suit bottom or clothing that provides equivalent protection against forceful water entry from being near jet thrust nozzles or falling into the water. Normal swimwear does not protect against forceful water entry into body cavities (See Owner's Manual).

Do not occupy swim platform when engine(s) is running. You could fall overboard.

YAMAHA
F3A-U416G-00 WARNING

Carbon monoxide (CO) can cause brain damage or death.

Engine exhaust contains odorless and colorless carbon monoxide gas.

Carbon monoxide will be around the back of the boat when engine is running.

Signs of carbon monoxide poisoning include nausea, headache, dizziness, drowsiness, and lack of consciousness.

Move to fresh air if you feel signs of carbon monoxide poisoning.

YAMAHA

F3A-U415R-00 ⚠ WARNING

Falling Hazard.

Falling on the deck or overboard may cause injury or death.

Hold on to the grips, remain seated and place feet on the deck when the boat is in motion.

Inspect system at least annually.

heading: Boat Description and Components / Boat glossary
text:
Boat glossary overview:

<PIC>
summary: Boat glossary overview:
caption_aux:
| TERM | DEFINITION |
|---|---|
| Bow | The front part of the boat. |
| Deck | The “floor” or upper structure which covers the hull. |
| Give-way | The vessel that must yield the right-of-way when two boats meet. |
| Gunwale | The meeting junction of the deck and hull; the upper edge around the boat. Pronounced “gunnel.” |
| Hatch | An opening in the deck that provides access below. |
| Helm | The steering console. |
| Hull | The basic part of the boat; the underside. |
| Lanyard | The cord or tether that connects the operator to the engine shut-off switch so the engine will stop if the operator accidentally leaves the helm. |
| PFD | A personal flotation device, also known as “life jacket.” |
| Planing | Traveling at a speed fast enough so the boat has leveled out and is skimming on top of the water. There is a wake. |
| Port | The left side of the boat. |
| Stand-on | The vessel with the right-of-way when two boats meet. |
| Starboard | The right side of the boat. |
| Stern | The back part of the boat. |
| Sub-planing | Traveling at a medium speed. The bow of the boat is out of the water, but you are still traveling through the water. There is a wake. |
| Transom | The vertical part of the stern. |
| Trolling | Traveling at idle speed, using little or no throttle. The boat is down in the water and it is not leaving a wake. |
| Wake | The visible track of disturbed water that the boat leaves behind as it moves in the water. |

text: <PIC>
caption_aux:
English:

| Problem | Solution |
|---|---|
| No light indicator. | Check the mains, plug, voltage, and fuse. In case of problems, call the Nespresso Club. |
| No coffee, no water. | First use: fill water tank with warm water (max. 55 °C) and run through machine according to instructions on page 9. Water tank is empty: Fill water tank. Descale if necessary; see Descaling section. |
| Coffee comes out very slowly. | Flow speed depends on the coffee variety. Descale if necessary; see Descaling section. |
| Coffee is not hot enough. | Preheat cup. Descale if necessary. |
| Capsule area is leaking (water in capsule container). | Position capsule correctly. If leakages occur, call the Nespresso Club. |
| Irregular blinking. | Send appliance to repair or call the Nespresso Club. |
| No coffee, just water runs out (despite inserted capsule). | In case of problems, call the Nespresso Club. |

Français:

| Problème | Solution |
|---|---|
| Pas de voyant lumineux. | Vérifier l’alimentation secteur, la prise, la tension et le fusible. En cas de problèmes, appeler le Club Nespresso. |
| Pas de café, pas d’eau. | Première utilisation: rincer la machine à l’eau chaude (max. 55 °C) conformément aux instructions de la page 9. Le réservoir d’eau est vide. Remplir le réservoir d’eau. Détartrer si nécessaire ; voir section Détartrage. |
| Le café s’écoule très lentement. | La vitesse d’écoulement dépend du type de café. Détartrer si nécessaire ; voir section Détartrage. |
| Le café n’est pas assez chaud. | Préchauffer la tasse. Détartrer si nécessaire. |
| Fuite dans la zone des capsules (de l’eau dans le réservoir à capsules). | Positionner la capsule correctement. Si la fuite persiste, appeler le Club Nespresso. |
| Clignotement à intervalles irréguliers. | Envoyer l’appareil en réparation ou appeler le Club Nespresso. |
| Il n’y a pas de café, seulement de l’eau qui s’écoule (malgré qu’une capsule soit insérée). | En cas de problème, appelez le Nespresso Club. |

| Emergencies | Possible Cause | Prevention/Solution | |---|---|---| | Gas leaking from cracked/cut/burned hose. | - Damaged hose. | - Turn off gas at LP cylinder or at source on natural gas systems. If anything but burned, replace valve/hose/regulator. If burned, discontinue use of product until a plumber has investigated cause and corrections are made. | | Gas leaking from LP cylinder. | - Mechanical failure due to rusting or mishandling. | - Replace LP cylinder. | | Gas leaking from LP cylinder valve. | - Failure of cylinder valve from mishandling or mechanical failure. | - Turn off LP cylinder valve. Return LP cylinder to gas supplier. | | Gas leaking between LP cylinder and regulator connection. | - Improper installation, connection not tight, failure of rubber seal. | - Turn off LP cylinder valve. Remove regulator from cylinder and visually inspect rubber seal for damage. See LP Cylinder Leak Test and Connecting Regulator to the LP Cylinder. | | Fire coming through control panel. | - Fire in burner tube section of burner due to blockage. | - Turn off control knobs and LP cylinder valve. Leave lid open to allow flames to die down. After fire is out and grill is cold, remove burner and inspect for spider nests or rust. See Natural Hazard and Cleaning the Burner Assembly pages. | | Grease fire or continuous excessive flames above cooking surface. | - Too much grease buildup in burner area. | - Turn off control knobs and LP cylinder valve. Leave lid open to allow flames to die down. After cooling, clean food particles and excess grease from inside firebox area, grease tray, and other surfaces. | | Problem | Possible Cause | Prevention/Solution | |---|---|---| | Burner(s) will not light using ignitor. (See Electronic Ignition Troubleshooting also) Continued on next page. | **GAS ISSUES:** - Trying to light wrong burner. - Burner not engaged with control valve. - Obstruction in burner. - No gas flow. - Vapor lock at coupling nut to LP cylinder. - Coupling nut and LP cylinder valve not fully connected. **ELECTRICAL ISSUES:** - Electrode cracked or broken; sparks at crack. - Electrode tip not in proper position. - Wire and/or electrode covered with cooking residue. - Wires are loose or disconnected. - Wires are shorting (sparking) between ignitor and electrode. - Dead battery. | - See instructions on control panel and in Use and Care section. - Make sure valves are positioned inside of burner tubes. - Ensure burner tubes are not obstructed with spider webs or other matter. See cleaning section of Use and Care. - Make sure LP cylinder is not empty. If LP cylinder is not empty, refer to “Sudden drop in gas flow.” - Turn off knobs and disconnect coupling nut from LP cylinder. Reconnect and retry. - Turn the coupling nut approximately one-half to three-quarters additional turn until solid stop. Tighten by hand only - do not use tools. - Replace electrode(s). Main Burners: - Tip of electrode should be pointing toward gas port opening on burner. The distance should be 1/8” to 1/4”. Adjust if necessary. Sideburner: - Tip of electrode should be pointing toward gas port opening on burner. the distance should be 1/8” to 3/16”. Adjust if necessary. - Clean wire and/or electrode with rubbing alcohol and clean swab. - Reconnect wires or replace electrode/wire assembly. - Replace ignitor wire/electrode assembly. - Replace with a new AA-size alkaline battery. | | Problem | Possible Cause | Prevention/Solution | |---|---|---| | Burner(s) will not light using ignitor. (See Electronic Ignition Troubleshooting also) | **ELECTRONIC IGNITION:**
- No spark, no ignition noise.
- No spark, some ignition noise.
- Sparks, but not at electrode or at full strength. | - See Section I of Electronic Ignition System.
- See Section II of Electronic Ignition System.
- See Section III of Electronic Ignition System. | | Burner(s) will not match light. | - See “GAS ISSUES:” on previous page.
- Match will not reach.
- Improper method of match-lighting. | - Use long-stem match (fireplace match).
- See “Match-Lighting” section of Use and Care. | | Sudden drop in gas flow or low flame. | - Out of gas.
- Excess flow valve tripped.
- Vapor lock at coupling nut/LP cylinder connection. | - Check for gas in LP cylinder.
- Turn off knobs, wait 30 seconds and light grill. If flames are still low, turn off knobs and LP cylinder valve. Disconnect regulator. Reconnect regulator and leak-test. Turn on LP cylinder valve, wait 30 seconds and then light grill.
- Turn off knobs and LP cylinder valve. Disconnect coupling nut from cylinder. Reconnect and retry. | | Flames blow out. | - High or gusting winds.
- Low on LP gas.
- Excess flow valve tripped. | - Turn front of grill to face wind or increase flame height.
- Refill LP cylinder.
- Refer to “Sudden drop in gas flow” above. | | Flare-up. | - Grease buildup.
- Excessive fat in meat.
- Excessive cooking temperature. | - Clean burners and inside of grill/firebox.
- Trim fat from meat before grilling.
- Adjust (lower) temperature accordingly. | | Persistent grease fire. | - Grease trapped by food buildup around burner system. | - Turn knobs to OFF. Turn gas off at LP cylinder. Leave lid in position and let fire burn out. After grill cools, remove and clean all parts. | | Flashback... (fire in burner tube(s)). | - Burner and/or burner tubes are blocked. | - Turn knobs to OFF. Clean burner and/or burner tubes. See burner cleaning section of Use and Care. | | Unable to fill LP cylinder. | - Some dealers have older fill nozzles with worn threads. | - The worn nozzles don’t have enough “bite” to engage the valve. Try a second LP dealer. | | One burner does not light from other burner(s). | - Grease buildup or food particles in end(s) of carryover tube(s). | - Clean carry-over tube(s) with wire brush. | | Problem (Ignition) | Possible Cause | Check Procedure | Prevention/Solution | |---|---|---|---| | SECTION I
No sparks appear at any electrodes when control knob turned to ignition/spark symbol; no noise can be heard from spark module. | - Battery not installed properly.
- Dead battery.
- Button assembly not installed properly.
- Faulty spark module. | - Check battery orientation.
- Has battery been used previously?
- Check to insure threads are properly engaged. Button should travel up and down without binding.
- If no sparks are generated with new battery and good wire connections, module is faulty. | - Install battery (make sure that “+” and “-” connectors are oriented correctly, with “+” end up and “-” end down.)
- Replace battery with new AA-size alkaline battery.
- Unscrew button cap assembly and reinstall, making sure threads are aligned and engaged fully.
- Replace spark module assembly. | | SECTION II
No sparks appear at any electrodes when control knob turned to ignition/spark symbol; noise can be heard from spark module. | - Output lead connections not connected. | - Are output connections on and tight? | - Remove and reconnect all output connections at module and electrodes. | | SECTION III
Sparks are present but not at all electrodes and/or not at full strength | - Output lead connections not connected.
- Electrical arc between output wires and grill frame.
- Weak battery.
- Electrodes are wet.
- Electrodes cracked or broken; sparks at electrode crack. | - Are output connections on and tight?
- If possible, observe grill in dark location. Operate ignition system and look for arcing between output wires and grill frame.
- All sparks present but weak or at slow rate.
- Has moisture accumulated on electrode and/or in burner ports?
- Inspect electrodes for cracks. | - Remove and reconnect all output connections at module and electrodes.
- If sparks are observed other than from burner(s), wire insulation may be damaged. Replace wires.
- Replace battery with a new AA-size alkaline battery.
- Use paper towel to remove moisture.
- Replace cracked or broken electrodes. |

Mowing Performance Tips

Using the Fast Throttle Setting

Using the Fast Throttle Setting: For best mowing and maximum air circulation, operate the engine at the FAST position. Air is required to thoroughly cut grass clippings, so do not set the height-of-cut so low as to totally surround the mower deck in uncut grass.

heading: Troubleshooting & Warranty / Troubleshooting / Before Calling For Service
text: BEFORE CALLING FOR SERVICE: Check the following list to be sure a service call is necessary. Reviewing additional information on items to check may prevent an unneeded service call. <PIC> <PIC>
summary: BEFORE CALLING FOR SERVICE: Check the following list to be sure a service call is necessary. Reviewing additional inform...
caption_aux:
| Problem | Possible Causes |
|---|---|
| If nothing on the oven operates... | - check for a blown circuit fuse or a tripped main circuit breaker.\n- check if oven is properly connected to electric circuit in house.\n- check that controls are set properly. |
| If the oven interior light does not work... | - the light bulb is loose or defective. |
| If oven will not cook... | - check that control panel was programmed correctly.\n- check that door is firmly closed.\n- check that Start Pad was touched.\n- check that timer wasn’t started instead of a cooking function. |
| If oven takes longer than normal to cook or cooks too rapidly... | - be sure the Power Level is programmed properly. |
| If the time of day clock does not always keep correct time... | - check that the power cord is fully inserted into the outlet receptacle.\n- be sure the oven is the only appliance on the electrical circuit. |
| If food cooks unevenly... | - be sure food is evenly shaped.\n- be sure food is completely defrosted before cooking.\n- check placement of aluminum foil strips used to prevent overcooking. |
| If food is undercooked... | - check recipe to be sure all directions (amount, time, and power levels) were correctly followed.\n- be sure microwave oven is on a separate circuit.\n- be sure food is completely defrosted before cooking. |
| If food is over cooked... | - check recipe to be sure all directions (amount, power level, time, size of dish) were followed. |
| If arcing (sparks) occur... | - be sure microwavable dishes were used.\n- be sure wire twist ties were not used.\n- be sure oven was not operated when empty.\n- make sure metal rack (if used) is properly installed on 4 supports. |
| If the display shows a time counting down but the oven is not cooking... | - check that door is firmly closed.\n- check that timer was not started instead of a cooking function. |
| If you vent fan starts automatically... | - If the temperature gets too hot around the microwave oven, the fan in the vent hood will automatically turn on at the LOW setting to cool the oven. It may stay on up to an hour to cool the oven. | WARNING

To avoid electrical shock which can cause severe personal injury or death, do not remove outer case at any time.
Only an authorized servicer should remove the outer case.

heading: Troubleshooting & Warranty / Troubleshooting / Questions And Answers
text: QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS: <PIC>
summary: QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS:
caption_aux:
| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Can I use a rack in my microwave oven so that I may reheat or cook in two rack positions at a time? | Only use the rack that is supplied with your microwave oven. Use of any other rack can result in poor cooking performance and/or arcing and may damage your oven. Do not use the rack when sensor cooking. |
| Can I use either metal or aluminum pans in my microwave oven? | Usable metal includes aluminum foil for shielding (use small, flat pieces). Never allow metal to touch walls or door. See page 6. |
| Sometimes the door of my microwave oven appears wavy. Is this normal? | This appearance is normal and does not affect the operation of your oven. |
| What are the humming noises I hear when my microwave oven is operating? | This is the sound the transformer makes when the magnetron tube cycles on and off. |
| Why does the dish become hot when I microwave food in it? | As the food becomes hot it will conduct the heat to the dish. Use hot pads to remove food after cooking. Dish also may not be microwave safe. See page 6. |
| What does standing time mean? | Standing time means that food should be taken out of the oven and covered for additional time after cooking. This process allows the cooking to finish, saves energy, and frees the oven for other purposes. In some dishes, the food temperature will continue to rise during this time. |
| Can I pop popcorn in my microwave oven? How do I get the best results? | Yes. Pop packaged microwave popcorn following manufacturer’s guidelines or use the preprogrammed Popcorn pad. See page 15. Do not use regular paper bags with unpopped corn - - use only pre-packaged, Microwavable Popcorn. Use the listening test by stopping the oven as soon as the popping slows to a pop every one or two seconds. Do not try to repop unpopped kernels. You can also use special microwave poppers: When using a popper, be sure to follow manufacturer’s directions. Do not pop popcorn in glass utensils. |
| Why does steam come out of the air exhaust vent? | Steam is normally produced during cooking. The microwave oven has been designed to vent this steam out the top vent. |

| Change display temperature °C / °F. | Press and hold + above Temp until the display indicates °C or °F. The temperature is displayed in the unit indicated. |
| Adjust and save custom cooking times and temperatures. | Once a Smart Program is selected, changes to the cooking time, temperature and pressure level are saved once the Smart Program begins. |
| Reset an individual smart program. | When in standby, press and hold one Smart Program button until the cooker returns to Standby and displays OFF.\n\nThe Smart Program’s pressure level, cooking time and temperature are restored to the factory default setting. |

caption_aux:
| Problem | Possible reason | Try this |
|---|---|---|
| The display remains blank after connecting the power cord. | Bad power connection or no power. | Inspect power cord for damage. If damage is noticed, contact Customer Care. Check outlet to make sure it is powered. |
| The display remains blank after connecting the power cord. | Cooker’s electrical fuse has blown. | Contact Customer Care. |
| Steam leaks from side of lid. | No sealing ring in the lid. | Install a sealing ring. |
| Steam leaks from side of lid. | The sealing ring is damaged or not installed properly. | Replace the sealing ring. |
| Steam leaks from side of lid. | Food debris attached to the sealing ring. | Remove the sealing ring and clean it thoroughly. |
| Steam leaks from side of lid. | The lid is not closed properly. | Open, then close the lid. |
| Steam leaks from side of lid. | The sealing ring rack is warped or off-center. | Remove the sealing ring from the lid, then check the sealing ring rack for bends or warps. Contact Customer Care. |
| Steam leaks from side of lid. | The inner pot rim may be misshapen. | Check for deformation and contact Customer Care. |
| Minor steam leaking or hissing from the steam release valve during the cook cycle. | Quick release button is not in the Seal position. | Flick the quick release button to make sure it is in the Seal position. |
| Minor steam leaking or hissing from the steam release valve during the cook cycle. | Cooker is regulating excess pressure. | This is normal; no action required. |
| Steam gushes from the steam release valve when the quick release button is in the Seal position. | Not enough liquid in the inner pot. | Add thin, water-based liquid to the inner pot according to its size: 6 Qt: 375 mL; 8 Qt: 500 mL |
| Steam gushes from the steam release valve when the quick release button is in the Seal position. | Pressure sensor control failure. | Contact Customer Care. |
| Steam gushes from the steam release valve when the quick release button is in the Seal position. | Steam release valve is not seated properly. | Flick the quick release button to make sure it is in the Seal position. | | Problem | Possible reason | Try this |
|---|---|---|
| Black smoke is coming from the air fryer lid. | CAUTION | Cancel the Smart Program, unplug the cooker and allow it to cool to room temperature. |
| Black smoke is coming from the air fryer lid. | Using an oil with a low smoke point. | Choose a neutral oil with a high smoke point, such as Canola, Avocado, Soybean, Safflower, or Rice Bran. |
| Black smoke is coming from the air fryer lid. | Food residue on the bottom of the inner pot or around the element on the air fryer lid. | Remove all accessories from the inner pot and clean the inner pot, air fryer lid, and all accessories thoroughly. |
| Black smoke is coming from the air fryer lid. | Appliance malfunction. | Contact Customer Care. |
| Error code appears on the display and the cooker beeps continuously. C1 / C2 / C6 / C6H / C6L | Faulty sensor. | Contact Customer Care. |
| Error code appears on the display and the cooker beeps continuously. C5 | Temperature is too high because the inner pot is not in the cooker base. | Press Cancel and wait for heating element to cool, make sure there are no foreign objects in cooker base; insert or reposition inner pot in cooker base and re-enter commands. |
| Error code appears on the display and the cooker beeps continuously. C5 | Temperature is too high. | Check for scorching on bottom of inner pot. Add thin, water-based liquid to the inner pot according to its size. |
| Error code appears on the display and the cooker beeps continuously. C7 | Heat element has failed. | Contact Customer Care. |
| Error code appears on the display and the cooker beeps continuously. C7 | Not enough liquid. | Add thin, water-based liquid to the inner pot according to its size |
| Error code appears on the display and the cooker beeps continuously. C7 | Quick release button is in the Vent position. | Flick quick release button to make sure it is in the Seal position. |
| Error code appears on the display and the cooker beeps continuously. Lid | Lid is not in the correct position for the selected program. | Open and close the lid. Do not use a lid when using Sauté. |
| Error code appears on the display and the cooker beeps continuously. Food burn | High temperature detected at bottom of inner pot; cooker automatically reduces the temperature to avoid overheating. | Starch deposits at the bottom of the inner pot may have blocked heat dissipation. Turn the cooker off, release pressure according to the recipe, and inspect the bottom of the inner pot. |
| Error code appears on the display and the cooker beeps continuously. PrSE | Pressure has accumulated during a non-pressure cooking program. | Press quick release button down until it clicks into Vent position. |

heading: 保养与清洁 / 日常清洁指引
text:

text:
若耳机或头显接口不洁，还可能出现噪音或声音中断。

镜片：仅使用专用柔软干布擦拭镜片。请勿使用纸巾等非镜片专用纸质产品。长时间接触水或灰尘可能损坏镜片并缩短其使用寿命。

遮光罩：将遮光罩从VR头显上取下，用水清洗。用软布完全擦干后再装回头显。将遮光罩上的凸点与头显上的13个孔对齐，重新安装即可。 <PIC>

通风口：使用吸尘器等工具清除通风口积聚的灰尘。

耳塞：将耳塞从立体声耳机上取下，用中性洗涤剂手洗。用软布完全擦干后再装回耳机。取下耳塞的详细说明，请参阅“更换耳塞”（第13页）。

heading: General Information / Important Labels / Warning Labels
text: Warning labels: <PIC> <PIC> <PIC>
summary: Warning labels:
caption_aux:
⚠ WARNING

To reduce the risk of SEVERE INJURY or DEATH:

- WEAR A PERSONAL FLOTATION DEVICE (PFD). All riders must wear a Coast Guard approved PFD that is suitable for personal watercraft (PWC) use.
- WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHING. Severe internal injuries can occur if water is forced into body cavities as a result of falling into water or being near jet thrust nozzle. Normal swimwear does not adequately protect against forceful water entry into rectum or vagina. All riders must wear a wet suit bottom or clothing that provides equivalent protection (See Owner’s Manual). Footwear, gloves, and goggles/glasses are recommended.
- KNOW BOATING LAWS. YAMAHA MOTOR CO., LTD. recommends a minimum operator age of 16 years old. Know the operator age and training requirements for your state. A boating safety course is recommended and may be required in your state.
- ATTACH ENGINE SHUT-OFF CORD (LANYARD) to wrist and keep it free from handlebars so that engine stops if operator falls off. After riding,

Figure labels:
- PFD
- Wet Suit Bottom

- RIDE WITHIN YOUR LIMITS AND AVOID AGGRESSIVE MANEUVERS to reduce the risk of loss of control, ejection, and collision. This is a high performance boat—not a toy. Sharp turns or jumping wakes or waves can increase the risk of back/spinal injury (paralysis), facial injuries, and broken legs, ankles, and other bones. Do not jump wakes or waves.
- DO NOT APPLY THROTTLE WHEN ANYONE IS AT REAR OF PWC—turn engine off or keep engine at idle. Water and/or debris exiting jet thrust nozzle can cause severe injury.
- KEEP AWAY FROM INTAKE GRATE while engine is on. Items such as long hair, loose clothing, or PFD straps can become entangled in moving parts resulting in severe injury or drowning.
- NEVER RIDE AFTER CONSUMING DRUGS OR ALCOHOL

heading: 功能调节 / 功能调节（高度 / 后仰 / 按摩）
text:
本椅子支持高度调节、椅背后仰锁定、腰枕按摩三项功能。

高度调节
向上拉起 “升降” 拉杆即可调节椅子高度，到达所需高度后松开 “升降” 拉杆。 <PIC>
调节高度时请将身体微微抬离座椅。 <PIC>

椅背后仰功能
向上拉起 “后仰” 拉杆，椅背角度可随人体动作独立倾斜。 <PIC>
向下按下 “后仰” 拉杆，椅背角度即可锁定。将椅背复位至正常位置时请靠在椅背上，否则椅背可能会快速回弹。 <PIC>

按摩功能
插入 USB 即可启用腰枕的按摩功能。 <PIC>

heading: 常见问题
text:
Q：使用一段时间后扶手变松怎么办？
A：大多数情况下，扶手和椅背的螺丝会在使用一段时间后松动，重新拧紧螺丝即可解决问题。

text:
穿着建议：穿着橡胶底运动鞋。穿着适合运动、活动自如的衣物。

1. 将脚踏板转到前位，脚掌中心对准脚踏板中心。膝盖应保持微弯。
2. 如腿部过直或脚无法踩到脚踏板，将立式单车座椅调低。如膝盖弯曲过度，将座椅调高。调节座椅前请先下车。松开并拉出座管上的调节旋钮，将座椅调至所需高度，松开旋钮使锁销卡入。

text:

text: 接触式心率传感器：接触式心率（CHR）传感器将心率信号发送至控制台。接触式心率传感器为把手的不锈钢部分。使用时将手舒适握住传感器区域，确保手同时接触传感器上下部分。握持稳固，不过紧或过松。必须双手同时接触传感器，控制台才能检测脉搏。控制台检测到四个稳定脉搏信号后，将显示初始心率。获取初始心率后，保持手部不动 10–15 秒，控制台将校准心率。

text:
获取初始心率后，保持手部不动 10–15 秒，控制台将校准心率。

多种因素会影响传感器检测心率信号的能力：

• 上肢肌肉（包括手臂）运动产生的电信号（肌肉干扰）可能影响脉搏检测。接触传感器时手部轻微移动也可能产生干扰。
• 老茧和护手霜可能形成绝缘层，降低信号强度。
• 部分使用者的心电图（EKG）信号强度不足，无法被传感器检测。
• 其他电子设备靠近可能产生干扰。

text:

环境因素（包括高楼、茂密森林、陡峭山坡和厚云层）可能干扰手表连接GPS卫星的能力。运动期间手表搜索GPS信号时，屏幕顶部会显示旋转的GPS图标。 <PIC>
为获得最佳效果，开始运动前等待健身追踪器找到信号。如运动期间健身追踪器丢失GPS信号，GPS图标会显示红色。手表会尝试重新连接。 <PIC>

text: 注意：前轮及前轴组装完成后，请检查车轮与把手管之间的间隙。若间隙过大、车轮定位不稳，建议在车轮与把手管之间加装额外垫片（不随产品提供）。加装垫片并重新安装前轴后，检查间隙是否最小化，同时确保车轮可自由转动。若车轮卡死，则减少一片垫片。

heading: 食物正确存放方法 / 食物存放注意事项 / 食物类型与热食存放
text:
• 请勿存放低温下易变质的食物，如香蕉、甜瓜。
• 热食需冷却后再存放。热食放入冰箱可能导致其他食物变质，并增加耗电量。
summary: • 请勿存放低温下易变质的食物，如香蕉、甜瓜。 • 热食需冷却后再存放。热食放入冰箱可能导致其他食物变质，并增加耗电量。

heading: 食物正确存放方法 / 食物存放注意事项 / 容器密封、通风与开门频率
text:
• 存放食物时请使用带盖容器，防止水分蒸发，保持食物口感与营养。
• 请勿用食物堵塞通风口。冷空气顺畅循环可保持冰箱温度均匀。
• 请勿频繁开门。开门会使热空气进入冰箱，导致温度升高。

heading: 食物正确存放方法 / 食物存放注意事项 / 门搁架、解冻食物与温敏物品
text:
• 切勿在门搁架上放置过多食物，以免门体无法完全关闭。
• 解冻后的食物请勿再次冷冻，会导致口感与营养流失。
• 请勿在冰箱内存放药品、科研材料或其他温度敏感物品。有严格温度控制要求的物品不得存放于本冰箱。

heading: 食物正确存放方法 / 食物存放注意事项 / 快速冷却与凝露处理
text:
• 如需快速冷却新放入的食物，将其放置在冷藏室中层抽屉，然后按下超强制冷按钮。
• 若冰箱放置在高温潮湿环境、频繁开门或放入大量蔬菜，可能产生凝露，不影响性能。用无绒布擦拭即可。

• 物品掉落或存放在冰箱后方。

冷冻食物结霜或冰晶：

• 门体未关严或包装卡住门体。
• 开门过于频繁或时间过长。
• 包装内结霜属正常现象。

heading: 安全信息 / 用电与接线安全
text:
发电机接入建筑物电气系统前，必须由持证电工在建筑物主配电箱内安装隔离（转换）开关。该开关为发电机电源的接入点，可选择使用发电机电源或市电电源为建筑物供电。这可防止市电故障或断电检修时发电机向市电线路反送电。反送电可能导致线路维修人员触电或受伤。若未安装隔离开关，恢复正常供电时还可能损坏发电机及建筑物电气系统。

AE00621 发动机

1. 拆下火花塞，向火花塞孔内注入约一汤匙SAE 10W30或20W40发动机油，重新安装火花塞。关闭点火开关，拉动反冲启动器数次，使机油覆盖气缸壁。
2. 拉动反冲启动器至感觉有压缩力时停止，防止气缸及阀门生锈。
3. 清洁发电机外部并涂抹防锈剂。
4. 将发电机存放在干燥、通风良好的地方，并盖上防护罩。
5. 发电机存放、搬运及运行时必须保持直立。 <PIC>

heading: 系统设置与运行 / 系统运行设置
text:
1 按模式键循环切换至下一个可用系统模式。
2 循环切换直至显示所需系统模式并保持激活状态。注：可用系统模式因型号及系统设置而异。 <PIC>
系统模式：

• 自动：温控器根据需要自动选择供暖或制冷。
• 供暖：温控器仅控制供暖系统。
• 制冷：温控器仅控制制冷系统。
• 应急供暖（仅适用于带辅助加热的热泵）：温控器控制辅助加热。不使用压缩机。
• 关闭：供暖和制冷系统关闭。若风扇设置为开启或循环模式，风扇仍可运行。
注：由于压缩机保护，供暖/制冷指示灯会闪烁5分钟。

heading: 程序日程与日常使用 / 程序日程
text:
您可每天设置四个时间段，工作日和周末可设置不同参数。建议使用预设设置（如下表所示），可有效降低供暖/制冷能耗。

• 起床——设置起床时间及早晨离家前的所需温度。
• 离家——设置离家时间及外出时的所需温度（通常为节能温度）。
• 回家——设置回家时间及晚上就寝前的所需温度。
• 睡眠——设置就寝时间及夜间所需温度（通常为节能温度）。 <PIC>

heading: 故障排除与警报 / 更换电池
text:
温控器需电池供电。电池低电量图标出现时请立即更换新电池。该图标会在电池耗尽前约两个月显示。即使未出现电池低电量图标，也应每年更换一次电池，或离家超过一个月前更换。若两分钟内完成电池更换，无需重新设置时间和日期。所有其他设置将永久存储在内存中，无需电池供电。 <PIC>
注：更换电池时建议使用碱性电池。

heading: 安全说明 / 人身安全
text:
以下说明适用于吹风机操作人员：

1. 操作人员必须阅读并理解本说明书内容。
2. 请勿穿着宽松衣物、佩戴围巾或项链，长发需束起，以免被吹风机旋转部件卷入造成伤害。
3. 饮酒、服药后或疲劳状态下请勿操作吹风机。
4. 禁止未成年人操作吹风机。

heading: 安全说明 / 吹风机操作安全
text:
1. 禁止无关人员及动物进入作业区域，即距操作人员 10 米范围内。
2. 吹风机可能高速喷射物体，物体反弹后可能击中操作人员，易造成严重眼部损伤。
3. 严禁将吹风机喷口对准人或动物。
4. 安装或拆卸配件及其他部件前必须先关闭发动机。
5. 任何防护装置缺失时严禁操作吹风机。
6. 严禁在通风不良的空间操作吹风机，避免吸入废气。
7. 加油前必须关闭发动机。

heading: 安全说明 / 其他安全措施
text:
1. 仅在合理时段操作吹风机，即避免在清晨或深夜扰民时段使用，遵守当地法规规定时段。通常建议周一至周六上午 9:00 至下午 5:00 使用。
2. 以完成作业所需的最低油门档位操作吹风机。
3. 操作前检查吹风机状态，重点检查消音器、进气口及空气滤清器。
4. 吹扫前先用耙子或扫帚松动地面杂物。
5. 多尘环境下，若有水可用软管轻微喷洒作业区域或使用喷雾附件。

7. 留意儿童、宠物、敞开的窗户及刚清洗的车辆，安全吹扫杂物。

text:

heading: 维护保养 / 化油器调节

heading: 维护保养 / 化油器调节
text:
• 工作原理：通过 L、H 油针调节油门开口对应的燃油供给量。顺时针旋入油针，空燃比变稀（燃油减少）；逆时针旋出，空燃比变浓（燃油增多）。稀混合气发动机转速升高，浓混合气转速降低。T 螺钉调节怠速转速，顺时针旋入怠速升高，逆时针旋出怠速降低。

text: • 消音器：注意！部分消音器配备催化转化器，详见“技术参数”确认您的设备是否配备。消音器设计用于降低噪音并将废气引导远离用户。废气温度较高且含有火花，朝向干燥易燃材料排放可能引发火灾。部分消音器配备专用火花阻隔网，若设备配备此类滤网需定期清洁，可用钢丝刷清洁。无催化转化器的消音器滤网每周清洁或按需更换；带催化转化器的消音器滤网每月检查清洁。

heading: 维护保养 / 系统检查与清洁
text:

## YOUR WARRANTY RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS

The EPA (U.S. Environmental Protection Agency), CARB (California Air Resources Board) and Husqvarna Forest & Garden are pleased to explain the emissions control system warranty on your 2001 and later small off-road engine. In U.S., new small off-road engines must be designed, built and equipped to meet the federal and California stringent anti-smog standards. Husqvarna Forest & Garden must warrant the emission control system on your small off-road engine for the periods of time listed below provided there has been no abuse, neglect or improper maintenance of your unit. Your emission control system includes Parts such as the carburetor and the ignition system. Where a warrantable condition exists, Husqvarna Forest & Garden will repair your small off-road engine at no cost to you. Expenses covered under warranty include diagnosis, parts and labor.

The 2001 and later small off-road engines are warranted for two years. If any emission related part on your engine (as listed above) is defective, the part will be repaired or replaced by Husqvarna Forest & Garden.

As the small off-road engine owner, you are responsible for the performance of the required maintenance listed in your Owner's Manual. Husqvarna Forest & Garden recommends that you retain all receipts covering maintenance on your small off-road engine, but Husqvarna Forest & Garden cannot deny warranty solely for the lack of receipts or for your failure to ensure the performance of all scheduled maintenance.

As the small off-road engine owner, you should, however, be aware that Husqvarna Forest & Garden may deny you warranty coverage if your small off-road engine or a part of it has failed due to abuse, neglect, improper maintenance, unapproved modifications or the use of parts not made or approved by the original equipment manufacturer.

You are responsible for presenting your small off-road engine to a Husqvarna Forest & Garden authorized servicing dealer as soon as a problem exists. The warranty repairs should be completed in a reasonable amount of time, not to exceed 30 days.

If you have any questions regarding your warranty rights and responsibilities, you should contact your nearest authorized servicing dealer or call Husqvarna Forest & Garden at 1-800-487-5963.

## WARRANTY COMMENCEMENT DATE

The warranty period begins on the date small off-road engine is delivered.

## LENGTH OF COVERAGE

Husqvarna Forest & Garden warrants to the initial owner and each subsequent purchaser that the engine is free from defects in materials and workmanship which cause the failure of a warranted part for a period of two years.

## WHAT IS COVERED

### REPAIR OR REPLACEMENT OF PARTS

Repair or replacement of any warranted part will be performed at no charge to the owner at an approved Husqvarna Forest & Garden servicing dealer.

If you have any questions regarding your warranty rights and responsibilities, you should contact your nearest authorized servicing dealer or call Husqvarna Forest & Garden at 1-800-487-5963.

### WARRANTY PERIOD

Any warranted part which is not scheduled for replacement as required maintenance, or which is scheduled only for regular inspection to the effect of "repair or replace as necessary" shall be warranted for 2 years. Any warranted part which is scheduled for replacement as required maintenance shall be warranted for the period of time up to the first scheduled replacement point for that part.

### DIAGNOSIS

The owner shall not be charged for diagnostic labor which leads to the determination that a warranted part is defective, if the diagnostic work is performed at an approved Husqvarna Forest & Garden servicing dealer.

### CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES

Husqvarna Forest & Garden may be liable for damages to other engine components caused by the failure of a warranted part still under warranty.

## WHAT IS NOT COVERED

All failures caused by abuse, neglect or improper maintenance are not covered.

### ADD-ON OR MODIFIED PARTS

The use of add-on or modified parts can be grounds for disallowing a warranty claim. Husqvarna Forest & Garden is not liable to cover failures of warranted parts caused by the use of add-on or modified parts.

## HOW TO FILE A CLAIM

Warranty services or repairs shall be provided at all Husqvarna Forest & Garden authorized servicing dealers.

避免碰撞：

●不要紧跟在其他摩托艇或船只后方。

heading: 重要安全说明与指南使用 / 重要信息
text:
以安全速度谨慎驾驶，与人员、物体及其他船只保持安全距离。
●不要紧跟在其他摩托艇或船只后方。
●不要靠近他人并向其喷水或溅水。
●避开有水下障碍物或浅水区的区域。
●EX / EX Sport：避免急转弯或其他让他人难以避让或判断你行驶方向的操作。
●EX Deluxe：避免急转弯、通过强力握紧智能减速电子倒挡（RiDE）手柄快速减速，以及其他让他人难以避让或判断你行驶方向的操作。

heading: 重要安全说明与指南使用 / 重要信息
text:
●EX Deluxe：避免急转弯、通过强力握紧智能减速电子倒挡（RiDE）手柄快速减速，以及其他让他人难以避让或判断你行驶方向的操作。

RiDE系统是控制发动机转速与倒挡闸门的电子系统，位于喷射推力喷嘴附近。左侧握把处的RiDE手柄可改变喷射推力方向，使摩托艇后退或进入空挡。RiDE系统在减速及低速操控（如下水、靠岸、停靠码头）时为驾驶者提供辅助。

text:

EX Deluxe：RiDE系统并非用于规避危险的制动装置。

heading: 重要安全说明与指南使用 / 如何使用本练习指南
text:
以下是各类速度的说明：
“拖曳速度”为最低操控速度，几乎不加油门。艇体沉入水中，无尾流。 <PIC>
“半滑航速度”为中等速度，艇首略微抬离水面，但仍在水中行驶，产生尾流。 <PIC>
“滑航速度”为较快速度，艇体更平稳，在水面滑行，产生尾流。 <PIC>

heading: 基础操作（练习1-3） / 练习2：发动机启动与停止
text:
目标：本练习教你了解发动机的启动与停止方式，以及启动后与怠速时摩托艇的状态。
技能：识别并执行发动机启动与停止的操控及步骤。 <PIC>

操作方法：
将摩托艇放入水中，在无杂草或杂物、水深至少60厘米（2英尺）的水域中练习，站立在艇旁操作。切勿在水深不足60厘米（2英尺）的水域操作，否则石子或沙子可能被吸入喷射口，导致叶轮损坏或发动机过热。

heading: 基础操作（练习1-3） / 练习2：发动机启动与停止
text:

训练1：启动发动机

1. 将发动机熄火绳①系在手腕上，将卡扣②插入发动机熄火开关③下方。确保熄火绳不缠绕车把，以防驾驶者落水时发动机无法停止。若绳子缠绕车把，卡扣可能无法脱落。
2. 按下启动开关④（绿色按钮）。不要握紧油门手柄，否则发动机无法启动。

heading: 基础操作（练习1-3） / 练习3：登艇与平衡
text:
目标：本练习训练你落水后在深水中登艇，以及扶正倾覆的摩托艇。重复练习直至能轻松完成。
技能：深水登艇与静止平衡。

操作方法：
先在近岸练习，再前往开阔水域。驾驶者体重越大，平衡艇体难度越高。练习时不启动发动机。将熄火绳系在手腕上，在水深至少齐胸的水域让艇漂浮。

训练1：登艇

1. 游至艇尾，双手放在登艇平台上，单手抓住扶手。 <PIC>
2. 拉身体至平台跪姿，再移至座位跨坐。

heading: 复杂环境与载客操作（练习8-9） / 练习8：穿越尾流与浪涌
text:
通常减速并“斜切”尾流（以一定角度穿越）可减轻冲击。驾驶时可能还会注意到另外两点：
一是连续穿越多道尾流或浪涌比单道更困难、更不平稳；
二是斜切尾流或浪涌时，艇体会试图偏离尾流或浪涌方向。以45°角穿越时可能不明显，但角度更小（如10°）时效果非常明显，需做好转向与平衡准备。 <PIC> <PIC> <PIC>

提示：

heading: 操作方法 / 发动机启动
text:
启动发动机前务必向泵内注满水。

1. 将燃油开关手柄置于“ON”位置。①“ON” <PIC>
2. 将发动机开关置于“ON”位置。①“ON” <PIC>
3. 将阻风门手柄置于关闭位置。①阻风门手柄 <PIC>
提示 热机启动无需关闭阻风门，将阻风门手柄置于工作位置即可。
4. 将油门手柄稍向右推。 <PIC>
5. 缓慢拉动反冲启动器至感觉受力，然后快速拉动。 <PIC> <PIC>
6. 发动机启动后预热，直至阻风门复位至工作位置也不会熄火。
7. 将阻风门手柄复位至工作位置。①工作位置 <PIC>
8. 将油门手柄调至所需位置。①降低发动机转速 ②提高发动机转速 <PIC>

heading: 操作方法 / 发动机停机与使用后处理
text:
发动机停机：

1. 将油门手柄完全向左推。 <PIC>
2. 将发动机开关置于“OFF”位置。①“OFF” <PIC>
3. 将燃油开关手柄置于“OFF”位置。①“OFF” <PIC>

使用后排水：冬季气温低于0℃（32℉）时，泵体内积水会结冰，可能导致水泵损坏。使用后请从底部排水口排空积水再存放。 <PIC>

高海拔运行：海拔超过4000英尺（1219米）时，发动机可能需要安装高海拔化油器套件以保证正常运行。如长期在该海拔以上使用，请联系当地经销商进行化油器改装。海拔4000英尺（1219米）以下应使用原厂配置，否则可能损坏发动机。

heading: 定期保养 / 机油与滤清器保养
text:

1. 将机器放置在水平面上，预热发动机数分钟后停机。
2. 取下机油加注口盖。
3. 在发动机下方放置接油盘，拆下放油螺塞，将机油完全排空。

heading: 定期保养 / 机油与滤清器保养
text:
提示 推荐发动机机油等级：API服务等级“SE”或“SF”。
注意 确保无异物进入曲轴箱。

空气滤清器：

1. 拆下空气滤清器盖及滤芯。
2. 用溶剂清洗滤芯并晾干。
3. 给滤芯上油并挤去多余油分，滤芯应湿润但不滴油。 <PIC> 推荐机油：泡沫空气滤清器专用油或SAE#20发动机机油。
注意 请勿拧绞滤芯，以免撕裂。
4. 将滤芯装入空气滤清器。
提示 确保滤芯密封面与滤清器贴合，无进气间隙。
注意 发动机不可无滤芯运行，否则会导致活塞及气缸过度磨损。
警告 吸烟或明火附近严禁使用溶剂。

heading: 首次使用与准备 / 餐具装载与碗篮 / 餐具适洗性与装载原则
text:
不适合在洗碗机中清洗的物品：
・切勿在洗碗机中清洗沾有烟灰、蜡烛残渣、抛光剂、染料、化学品等的餐具。
・请勿清洗铁制器具，以免生锈或在其他物品上留下污渍。
・请勿清洗带有木质或骨质手柄、黏合部件、不耐热部件的银质餐具、刀具，以及铜和镀锡容器。瓷器的装饰花纹以及铝制和银质器具在洗碗机中清洗后可能会褪色或失去光泽，就像手洗一样。

text:

餐具放入洗碗机：只有有序放置餐具，才能在能耗、洗涤和烘干效果方面实现洗碗机的最佳使用。

heading: 维护与清洁 / 日常维护 / 清洁频率、表面与内部清洁
text:
定期清洁可延长产品使用寿命，减少常见故障。进行任何清洁操作前，请拔掉产品电源并关闭水龙头。请勿使用研磨性物质清洁。过滤器和喷淋臂至少每周清洁一次。

产品外表面清洁：用温和清洁剂和软布轻轻清洁产品外表面和门封条。控制面板仅用软布擦拭。
机器内部清洁：根据脏污程度，空载运行预洗程序（不加洗涤剂）或长程序（加洗涤剂）清洁机器内部和内胆。若机器内积水，按照取消程序章节的操作排水。若无法排水，清洁机器底部堆积的残渣，疏通水路。

heading: 维护与清洁 / 日常维护 / 过滤器与滤网清洁
text:
过滤器清洁：为保证机器高效运行，至少每周清洁一次过滤器。检查过滤器上是否有食物残渣。若有残渣，取出并在流水下彻底清洁。

1. 逆时针旋转微过滤器（3）和粗过滤器（2）组件，从底座（A）中拉出。 <PIC>
2. 拉出金属 / 塑料过滤器（1）（B）。 <PIC>
3. 向内按压粗过滤器上的两个卡爪，将粗过滤器与组件分离（C）。 <PIC>
4. 用刷子在自来水下清洁所有三个过滤器。

heading: 维护与清洁 / 日常维护 / 过滤器与滤网清洁
text:
进水管滤网清洁：安装在进水管上的滤网可防止市政供水或自备水系统中的杂质（沙、污垢、铁锈等）损坏机器。定期检查滤网和水管，必要时清洁。

1. 关闭水龙头并拆下水管。
2. 取出滤网后在自来水下清洁。
3. 将清洁后的滤网装回水管原位。
4. 将水管装回水龙头。

heading: 故障排除 / 运行故障 / 机器启动、排水、泡沫与异味问题
text:
加注亮碟剂时注意不要洒入机器，用纸巾 / 毛巾清洁溢出的亮碟剂。
> > 亮碟剂盒盖未关。添加亮碟剂后确保亮碟剂盒盖关闭。
> > ・机器内有异味
> > 新机器有特殊气味，使用几次后会消失。

text:
设备门关闭时，热空气会从控制面板上方的开孔排出。请勿堵塞排气孔。

heading: 安全与环保 / 重要安全说明 / 高温烫伤、火灾与烹饪风险防范
text:
• 过热油脂极易起火。烹饪富含油脂的食物时请务必保持警惕。
• 烘干食物期间，切勿让设备无人看管运行。
• 烹饪时若使用酒精饮品（如朗姆酒、干邑、葡萄酒），请注意酒精在高温下会挥发。因此，酒精蒸汽接触电加热元件时可能引发火灾。

text:
节能

• 仅在烹饪表或食谱要求时才预热烤箱。

heading: 使用与操作 / 通用建议 / 首次使用前准备
text:
使用前：

• 取下配件上的纸板防护件、保护膜及不干胶标签。
• 将配件从烤箱中取出，以200℃空烤约一小时，去除绝缘材料及防护油脂产生的异味和烟雾。
summary: 使用前： • 取下配件上的纸板防护件、保护膜及不干胶标签。 • 将配件从烤箱中取出，以200℃空烤约一小时，去除绝缘材料及防护油脂产生的异味和烟雾。

• 请勿在烤箱门上放置重物，以免损坏。

• 请勿用铝箔纸覆盖烤箱内部。
• 请勿向热烤箱内倒水，否则可能损坏搪瓷涂层。
• 请勿拖拽锅具划过烤箱底部，以免损坏搪瓷涂层。
• 确保其他设备的电源线不接触烤箱高温部位或被烤箱门挤压。
• 请勿将烤箱暴露在露天环境中。

heading: 烹饪指南与技巧 / 推荐使用与技巧 / 甜点制作技巧
text:
甜点

• 精致甜点使用常规功能单层烹饪。使用深色金属蛋糕模，并始终放置在随附烤架上。如需多层同时烹饪，选择热风功能，错开蛋糕模位置，保证热空气循环最佳。
• 检查蓬松蛋糕是否熟透：将牙签插入蛋糕中心，拔出后无粘连即已熟透。
• 若使用不粘蛋糕模，请勿涂抹边缘黄油，否则蛋糕边缘可能无法均匀蓬松。
• 若蛋糕烹饪过程中塌陷，下次适当降低温度，可减少面糊液体用量并轻柔搅拌。
• 夹心湿润甜点（如芝士蛋糕、水果派）使用“热风烘焙”功能（如有）。若蛋糕底部过湿，降低层架高度，并在倒入馅料前撒上面包糠或饼干屑。

heading: 烹饪指南与技巧 / 推荐使用与技巧 / 披萨与发酵功能
text:
披萨
烤盘轻微刷油，保证披萨底酥脆。烹饪至三分之二时间时再撒马苏里拉芝士。

发酵功能（仅限特定型号）
建议面团放入烤箱前用湿布覆盖。使用该功能，面团发酵时间比室温（20‑25℃）缩短约三分之一。1千克披萨面团发酵时间约为一小时。

text:
烤箱不工作：

• 检查市电是否正常，烤箱是否已接通电源。
• 关闭烤箱后重新开机，查看故障是否仍存在。

烤箱门无法打开：

• 关闭烤箱后重新开机，查看故障是否仍存在。
• 重要提示：自清洁期间，烤箱门将锁定无法打开。等待自动解锁（参见“带高温自清洁功能烤箱的清洁程序”章节）。

电子程序器不工作：

• 若显示屏显示字母“F”加数字，请联系最近的售后服务中心，并说明字母“F”后的数字。

heading: 故障排查与售后服务 / 售后服务 / 联系售后服务前的检查与信息准备
text:
联系售后服务前：

1. 借助“故障排查指南”中的建议，尝试自行解决问题。
2. 关闭设备电源后重新开机，查看故障是否仍存在。

若经上述检查故障仍存在，请联系最近的售后服务中心。请务必说明：

• 故障简要描述；
• 烤箱类型及精确型号；
• 服务编号（铭牌上Service字样后的编号），位于烤箱腔体右侧边缘（开门可见）。服务编号也标注在保修手册上；
• 您的完整地址；
• 您的联系电话。

如需维修，请联系授权售后服务中心（以确保使用原厂配件并正确维修）。

heading: 电池与充电器 / 重要充电注意事项
text:
1.环境温度在65°F至75°F（18°C-24°C）时为电池组充电，可获得最长寿命和最佳性能。不要在环境温度低于40°F（4.5°C）或高于105°F（40.5°C）时充电。这一点很重要，可防止电池组严重损坏。
2.充电时，充电器和电池组可能会发热。这是正常状态，不表示存在故障。为方便使用后电池组冷却，避免将充电器或电池组放在高温环境中，如金属棚屋或无隔热层的拖车。

heading: 电池与充电器 / 壁挂安装与存放建议
text:
壁挂安装：这些充电器可壁挂或直立放置在桌面或工作台面。如需壁挂，将充电器安装在电源插座可及范围内。使用至少1英寸（25.4毫米）长的石膏板螺钉牢固安装充电器，螺钉拧入木材至合适深度，留出约7/32英寸（5.5毫米）的螺钉外露部分。

存放建议：1.最佳存放场所为阴凉干燥处，远离阳光直射和过冷过热环境。2.长期存放时，建议将充满电的电池组存放在阴凉干燥处、脱离充电器，以获得最佳效果。注：电池组不应完全耗尽电量存放。使用前需重新充电。保存这些说明以供日后使用。

heading: 操作指南 / 电池组的安装与拆卸
text:
注：为获得最佳效果，确保电池组充满电。
将电池组（K）对准工具手柄内导轨，滑入手柄直至电池组牢固就位且不会松脱。
拆卸电池组时，按下释放按钮（J），将电池组从工具手柄中平稳拔出。按照本手册充电器部分所述插入充电器。 <PIC>

heading: 操作指南 / 钻孔
text:

heading: 操作指南 / 钻孔
text:
立即松开扳机，将钻头从工件中取出，查明堵转原因。不要反复扣动扳机尝试启动堵转的电钻——这可能损坏电钻。
6.为最大程度减少堵转或钻透材料，减轻电钻压力，让钻头平稳钻透最后部分。
7.将钻头从钻孔中拉出时保持电机运转。这有助于防止卡钻。

heading: 操作指南 / 拧螺丝
text:
1.使用变速拨杆选择所需速度/扭矩范围，匹配计划作业的速度和扭矩。
2.将扭矩调节环（C）转至所需位置。注：使用使紧固件拧入所需深度的最低扭矩设置。数字越小，扭矩输出越低。 <PIC>
3.将所需紧固件附件像钻头一样装入夹头。
4.在废料或工件不显眼位置进行试操作，确定扭矩调节环的合适位置。
5.始终从低扭矩设置开始，然后逐步调高，避免损坏工件或紧固件。

heading: 操作指南 / 冲击钻孔
text:
1.使用变速拨杆选择所需速度/扭矩范围，匹配计划作业的速度和扭矩。将调节环（C）转至冲击钻符号。 <PIC> 重要：仅使用额定冲击钻孔的硬质合金或砌体钻头。
2.施加适当力度，防止冲击钻过度弹跳或“脱离”钻头。用力过大会导致钻孔速度变慢、过热，降低钻孔效率。
3.垂直钻孔，保持钻头与工件成直角。钻孔时不要对钻头施加侧向压力，否则会导致钻头排屑槽堵塞，钻孔速度变慢。
4.钻深孔时，如果冲击速度开始下降，在工具仍运转的情况下将钻头部分拉出孔外，帮助清除孔内碎屑。注：钻孔时粉尘平稳均匀排出表示钻孔速度合适。

heading: 基础拍摄与打印 / 拍摄基本操作
text:
本节介绍基本拍摄操作。顺时针转动镜头环（电源开关）开机。 <PIC> 手持相机并确认最终图像的构图。 <PIC>
选择拍摄模式或进行图像效果设置。（第53至57页）半按快门对焦。

相机内存注意事项：

heading: 规格参数与故障排除 / 规格参数
text:
相机：
• 图像传感器：1/4英寸CMOS原色滤镜
• 有效像素：1920×1920
• 存储介质：内置内存、microSD/microSDHC存储卡

3. 每月清洁设备及预过滤网 1-2 次。

heading: 清洁、维护、存放与故障排除 / 灰尘传感器清洁、长期存放与故障排除
text:
1. 双手握住设备上盖并向上拉起。 <PIC>
2. 握住背部滤网盖把手并向前拉出。 <PIC>
3. 拆下设备右侧灰尘传感器盖。 <PIC>
4. 用蘸少量水的棉签擦拭灰尘传感器镜头和进风口，再用干净干棉签彻底擦干。 <PIC>
5. 装回灰尘传感器盖。装回滤网盖。将设备上盖标识朝前装回。

请勿使用丙酮、酒精等强腐蚀性化学试剂擦拭传感器部件，以免损坏镜头。

长期存放：

1. 晴天运行设备 1 小时，拔下电源插头，晾干设备内部。
2. 遮盖设备并存放在干燥、无阳光直射的地方。

heading: 重要安全说明 / 操作与日常安全 / 清洁维修、特殊用途限制、风口安全与遥控器电池安全
text:
・切勿对电池充电或拆解电池，否则可能导致爆炸、火灾或严重受伤。
・若遥控器电池漏液，立即停止使用，若衣物或皮肤接触到漏液，用清水冲洗，否则可能导致严重受伤。
・若不慎误食电池漏液，彻底漱口并立即就医，否则可能导致严重的健康问题。
summary: ・切勿对电池充电或拆解电池，否则可能导致爆炸、火灾或严重受伤。 ・若遥控器电池漏液，立即停止使用，若衣物或皮肤接触到漏液，用清水冲洗，否则可能导致严重受伤。 ・若不慎误食电池漏液，彻底漱口并立即就医，否则可能导致严重的健康问题。

本空调配备多种实用的高级功能。

快速调节室内温度（极速制冷 / 制热模式）
该模式可在夏季快速冷却室内空气，或在冬季快速提升室内温度。

1. 按下开 / 关键开启电源。
2. 按下极速键。 <PIC>

• 极速制冷模式下，空调将以 18 摄氏度的温度强风出风 30 分钟。
• 极速制热模式下，空调将以 30 摄氏度的温度强风出风 30 分钟。
注：循环、自动或自动转换模式下，无法使用此功能。

制冷和除湿运行时，室内机内部会产生水汽，可使用自清洁功能去除水汽。

1. 按下自清洁键，显示屏上会显示自清洁标识。 <PIC>

• 若关闭电源，风扇将继续运行 30 分钟，对室内机内部进行清洁。

本产品搭载的等离子滤网可彻底去除吸入空气中的微小污染物，输送洁净清新的空气。

1. 按下开 / 关键开启电源。

heading: 维护保养 / 滤网清洁与保养要求 / 维护前注意事项与空气滤网清洁
text:
定期清洁产品，以保持最佳运行性能，防止设备出现故障。部分配件可能因机型不同而未配备。

进行任何维护操作前，请关闭电源并拔下电源线，否则可能导致触电。清洁滤网时，切勿使用 40 摄氏度以上的热水，以免造成滤网变形或变色。清洁滤网时，切勿使用挥发性物质，以免损坏产品表面。
注：请定期清洁室外机的热交换器盘管，盘管积垢可能会降低运行效率，增加能耗。

heading: 维护保养 / 滤网清洁与保养要求 / 维护前注意事项与空气滤网清洁
text:
注：请定期清洁室外机的热交换器盘管，盘管积垢可能会降低运行效率，增加能耗。

建议每两周清洁一次空气滤网，必要时可增加清洁频率。 <PIC>

1. 关闭电源并拔下电源线。
2. 打开前盖板，轻轻掀起盖板两侧即可。 <PIC> 功能会根据机型有所调整。
3. 握住空气滤网的把手，轻轻向上提起，将其从机身中取出。 <PIC> 功能会根据机型有所调整。
4. 用吸尘器清理滤网，或用温水冲洗，若滤网污垢较难清理，可在温水中加入洗涤剂清洗。
5. 将滤网置于阴凉处晾干。

heading: 故障排除 / 自诊断与报修检查 / 自诊断提示与报修前检查
text:
本产品内置自诊断功能，若发生故障，室内机指示灯会以 2 秒为间隔闪烁，出现此情况请联系当地经销商或服务中心。

报修前，请先检查以下事项，若问题仍未解决，再联系当地服务中心。
<PIC>
<PIC>
summary: 本产品内置自诊断功能，若发生故障，室内机指示灯会以 2 秒为间隔闪烁，出现此情况请联系当地经销商或服务中心。 报修前，请先检查以下事项，若问题仍未解决，再联系当地服务中心。
caption_aux:
| Problem | Possible causes | Corrective action |
|---|---|---|
| There is a burning smell and a strange sound coming from the unit. | - | Turn off the air conditioner, unplug the power cord and contact the service center. |
| Water leaks from the indoor unit even when the humidity level is low. | - | Turn off the air conditioner, unplug the power cord and contact the service center. |
| The power cord is damaged or generating excessive heat. | - | Turn off the air conditioner, unplug the power cord and contact the service center. |
| A switch, a circuit breaker (safety, ground) or a fuse is not operated properly. | - | Turn off the air conditioner, unplug the power cord and contact the service center. |
| The air conditioner does not work. | The air conditioner is unplugged. | Check whether the power cord is plugged into the outlet. |
| The air conditioner does not work. | A fuse is blown or the power supply is blocked. | Replace the fuse or check if the circuit breaker has tripped. |
| The air conditioner does not work. | A power failure has occurred. | Turn off the air conditioner when a power failure occurs. When the power is restored, wait 3 minutes, and then turn on the air conditioner. |

|---|---|---|

注：首次使用时，机器可能需数秒才出蒸汽。水需通过过滤器流入加热器。该延迟仅首次使用出现。

text:
要开始使用蓝牙驱动程序，请双击系统托盘中的蓝牙图标。 <PIC>

1. 蓝牙初始配置向导将启动。请按照屏幕上的说明完成配置。
2. 蓝牙配置完成后，将出现以下 HID 界面并开始搜索蓝牙设备。 <PIC>
3. 点击您要连接的 HID 设备。然后按照屏幕上的说明启用所选设备。

关于蓝牙图标：蓝牙图标用于显示接收器状态。

1. 红色图标：未插入接收器。

heading: 故障排除
text:
若您的蓝牙鼠标出现任何问题，请检查以下事项：
・检查系统要求，确保您的系统兼容。
・检查鼠标电池是否安装正确。确保电池正负极与鼠标电池仓内的标识一致。
・当鼠标 LED 指示灯亮起红色时，表示电量低。请立即更换新电池。
